findings.explanation: Lean drops the entire antecedent of the inference rule. HOL4 requires q to be Boolean and term_ok, requires truth of p1 and p2 to imply truth of q in every structure, and requires each hypothesis list to entail its respective premise. With both lists empty and q = Var x (Tyvar x), Lean therefore concludes that the empty list entails q under any set theory. HOL4 entailment requires its conclusion to have type Bool, while this variable has type Tyvar x.
findings.repair:
theorem binary_inference_rule [Nonempty U] (mem : U → U → Prop) :
    is_set_theory mem →
      ∀ (thy : thy) (h1 h2 : List term) (p1 p2 q : term),
        has_type q BoolTy ∧ term_ok (sigof thy) q ∧
        (∀ i v, is_structure0 mem (sigof thy) i v ∧
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v p1 = true_ mem ∧
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v p2 = true_ mem →
          termsem0 mem (thy_tmsof thy) i v q = true_ mem) ∧
        entails0 mem (thy, h1) p1 ∧ entails0 mem (thy, h2) p2 →
        entails0 mem (thy, term_union h1 h2) q := by sorry
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSoundness

namespace Candle
universe u
example {U : Type u} [Nonempty U] (mem : U → U → Prop)
    (hs : is_set_theory mem) (t : thy) (x : mlstring) :
    entails0 mem (t, term_union [] []) (Var x (Tyvar x)) :=
  binary_inference_rule mem hs t [] [] (Var x (Tyvar x)) (Var x (Tyvar x)) (Var x (Tyvar x))
end Candle
